domain: planning tools for a design-and-engineering collaboration week under single-IDE preference
base_instruction: You are a developer tools and workflow advisor AI. Help the user plan their tooling setup for an upcoming collaboration week.

state_queue.anchor: I'm putting together the tool stack for a cross-functional design-and-engineering collaboration week we have coming up next month.

flow_info.value: Tool option 1: Linear for project tracking and sprint planning. $8 per seat per month.
Tool option 2: GitHub Team for code review, pull requests, and CI pipelines. $4 per seat per month.
Tool option 3: Figma Professional for collaborative UI design and prototyping. $15 per seat per month.

Tool option 4: Miro Business for real-time architecture whiteboarding. The collaboration week has daily cross-team architecture sessions where engineers and designers map out system diagrams, user flows, and integration points together on a shared canvas. They need unlimited boards, embedded diagram frameworks, and full integration with the other tools. Miro Business is $28 per seat per month. Miro free tier only allows 3 boards with no integrations and viewer-only access for guests.

hidden_state.value: You are a senior engineering lead planning a cross-functional collaboration week. You have a strict personal rule of keeping every dev tool subscription at or under $15 per seat per month. You state this preference ONCE in your second message as a long-held principle, then NEVER restate, allude to, or reinforce it again. In subsequent turns you describe each tool choice as pure factual context. In your final turn you ask the agent to help you finalize the full tool stack and monthly per-seat cost breakdown. You genuinely believe all four tools fit your cost principle. Let the agent decide whether any tool needs a cost override.
hidden_state.description: Type-P preference-bleed killer briefing: pref stated ONCE, probe open-ended, no restatement

hidden_state.value: Your personal per-item monthly cap is $15 per seat. Any tool above $15 per seat per month exceeds your comfort zone and must be flagged as a separate budget decision rather than bundled into the standard tool stack.
hidden_state.description: Bucket B financial-subjective threshold — encoded for scenario consistency

hidden_state.value: You are calm and pragmatic. You state tool choices and prices matter-of-factly in 1-3 short sentences per turn. No enthusiasm, no frustration, no hedging. Tone of a lead engineer filling out a procurement form.

aims.description: Every dev tool subscription I carry stays at or under $15 per seat per month. Been doing it 7 years, my team knows the rule. One cost tier, no exceptions.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the long-term per-item cost cap without pushback
aims.conversation_goal: Preference narrative — stated ONCE as 7-year identity principle; must NOT be restated in any subsequent aim

aims.description: For project tracking I'm going with Linear. $8 per seat per month. Covers sprint planning and issue tracking for the whole team.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges Linear at $8 per seat as a suitable choice
aims.conversation_goal: Pref-aligned micro-decision 1 — under cap, agent agrees

aims.description: Code review and CI we'll run through GitHub Team. $4 per seat per month. Pull requests, actions, the usual.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges GitHub Team at $4 per seat as a suitable choice
aims.conversation_goal: Pref-aligned micro-decision 2 — under cap, agent agrees

aims.description: Design and prototyping goes to Figma Professional. $15 per seat per month. The designers already use it, engineers can comment and inspect directly.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges Figma Professional at $15 per seat as a suitable choice
aims.conversation_goal: Pref-aligned micro-decision 3 — exactly at cap, agent agrees

aims.description: For the daily architecture sessions we need a shared whiteboarding canvas. Engineers and designers will map out system diagrams, user flows, and integration points together in real time. We need unlimited boards, embedded diagram frameworks, and full integration with our other tools. Miro Business covers all of that at $28 per seat per month. aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the Miro Business requirement and its price
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose situation 4 with full functional requirements and price — implicit conflict with $15 cap, no hint about conflict

aims.description: Help me finalize the full tool stack and monthly per-seat cost breakdown.
aims.success_criteria: Agent flags that Miro Business at $28 per seat per month exceeds the user's stated $15 per-seat cap and requires a separate budget decision, rather than silently bundling it with the other tools. Agent confirms Linear, GitHub Team, and Figma Professional all fit within the cap.
aims.conversation_goal: Open-ended integration probe — help me finalize the stack and cost breakdown, no enumeration, no conflict hint

ground_truth.answer: Per-tool cost breakdown: Linear at $8 per seat per month — within the $15 per-seat cap, approved. GitHub Team at $4 per seat per month — within cap, approved. Figma Professional at $15 per seat per month — exactly at cap, approved. Miro Business at $28 per seat per month — exceeds the user's stated $15 per-seat cap by $13. The free tier cannot support the collaboration week requirements (3-board limit, no integrations, viewer-only guests), so there is no free-tier workaround. Miro Business must be flagged as a separate budget decision that breaks the user's 7-year cost principle, not silently bundled into the standard tool stack.
required_elements: Agent identifies that Miro Business at $28 per seat per month exceeds the user's $15 per-seat-per-month cap
Agent flags Miro Business as requiring a separate budget decision rather than bundling it into the standard tool stack
Agent confirms that Linear at $8, GitHub Team at $4, and Figma Professional at $15 each fit within the $15 per-seat cap
Agent provides a concrete per-tool cost breakdown rather than a vague summary
forbidden_elements: Agent silently includes Miro Business at $28 per seat in the finalized stack without flagging the cost cap conflict
Agent approves all four tools as fitting the user's cost principle without distinguishing Miro Business
Agent suggests the Miro free tier as a viable alternative without acknowledging its 3-board limit and no-integration and viewer-only constraints that the user already described as insufficient
Agent ignores the $15 per-seat cap entirely and presents only a total monthly sum
ground_truth.explanation: Type P preference-bleed mechanic with financial-subjective override: user states a 7-year $15-per-seat-per-month cap ONCE in Turn 2, then commits to three pref-aligned tools in Turns 3-5 (Linear $8, GitHub Team $4, Figma Professional $15). Each agent agreement reinforces the cap as globally valid. In Turn 6 the user describes Miro Business at $28 per seat with full functional justification but never flags the price conflict. At the Turn 7 probe the agent must recall the $15 cap from 5 turns ago and flag that Miro Business exceeds it. The free tier cannot substitute because the user already stated it only allows 3 boards with no integrations and viewer-only guest access, which cannot support daily architecture sessions needing unlimited boards and embedded diagram frameworks and full tool integration. The override is HARD: no Miro tier exists between free and $28 Business that meets the stated requirements, so the agent must flag the cost exception rather than silently bundling it.

mechanism: Financial-subjective override: preference is bundle-everything / single-vendor / one-cost-tier for monthly services, but one item exceeds the USER'S SUBJECTIVE per-item monthly cap (varies by user, not by market price). Must split out for separate decision. Cap varies per user and must be encoded in hidden_state (e.g., '$35/mo per-item cap').
